As one of the company's first engineers, you will own the AI layer of the product: the models, the pipelines, and the evaluations that determine whether what ships actually works for merchants.
 



  





 This is a production engineering role, not a research position — you will write and ship production code to real customers every week and be the team's go\-to expert when anything model\-related breaks.
 



  





 The architecture decisions you make in your first months will shape the platform for years, and you will work closely with the founding team and product engineers to turn ambiguous merchant problems into reliable AI features.
 



  





 Key Responsibilities
 



  




* Own the end\-to\-end AI system, including prompting, retrieval (RAG), tool use, and agent orchestration across the merchant\-facing assistant.
* Build evaluation harnesses before building features, so every model or prompt change is measured against defined quality benchmarks rather than intuition.
* Detect and prevent regressions through automated LLM evaluation pipelines integrated into the release process.
* Reduce inference latency and cost to levels that are sustainable at merchant scale, not just in demos.
* Diagnose ambiguous product problems to determine whether the root cause is a model, data, or UX issue — then drive the fix.
* Apply fine\-tuning selectively where it delivers measurable gains over prompting and retrieval.
* Ship to production weekly and monitor real\-world model behavior through logging, analytics, and user feedback.
* Make foundational architecture decisions for the AI stack and document the trade\-offs behind them.
* Collaborate with full\-stack engineers working in React, TypeScript, and Node.js to integrate AI capabilities across the product.

**Join a fast\-growing seed\-stage AI startup building intelligent systems for complex, high\-stakes insurance investigations.** 




  





 This team is building a claims intelligence platform that helps investigators uncover fraud across property and casualty insurance. By connecting information across claims, businesses, contractors, individuals, phone numbers, documents, and other data sources, the platform turns fragmented information into evidence investigators can act on.
 



  





 The company has already built substantial backend, document\-processing, data\-extraction, and traditional machine learning infrastructure. With seven\-figure customer agreements, the business is now investing heavily in the next layer of its platform: production\-grade AI agents capable of carrying out sophisticated investigative workflows.
 



  





**What You’ll Do** 



* Design, build, and iterate on production AI agents, including their tools, context, orchestration, prompts, and guardrails.
* Own the evaluation framework for agent performance, from defining what “good” looks like through to measuring it systematically.
* Partner directly with fraud investigators to create high\-quality golden datasets based on real investigative workflows.
* Build LLM\-as\-judge, deterministic, and rule\-based graders to evaluate agent outputs.
* Develop regression suites that validate prompt, model, and orchestration changes before they reach production.
* Create quality dashboards that make agent performance and failure modes understandable across engineering, product, and operations teams.
* Instrument production agents for traces, tool usage, cost, latency, and other critical performance metrics.
* Turn real\-world production failures into new evaluation cases and continuously improve the system.
* Evaluate new foundation models and providers end\-to\-end, then own the technical rollout when the team decides to switch.
* Partner closely with backend engineers on the data and service infrastructure agents depend on.
* Work with Operations and investigators to understand how AI behaves in real, sometimes adversarial, investigative environments.
* Build with a high bar for precision: incorrect findings can have genuine consequences for the people involved in a claim.



  





**What You’ll Bring** 



* Strong Python engineering skills and a disciplined approach to testing and software quality.
* Hands\-on experience shipping LLM\-powered agents into production environments.
* A clear understanding of why production agents succeed or fail beyond simply getting a prototype working.
* Experience building evaluation datasets, graders, regression suites, or evaluation harnesses for LLM applications.
* Evidence that evaluation results have directly influenced product, model, or engineering decisions you’ve made.
* Strong knowledge of tool\-using agents, agent orchestration, and emerging agent protocols and frameworks.
* Experience moving comfortably between rapid experimentation and production hardening.
* The judgment to know when a lightweight prototype is sufficient and when reliability, observability, and testing need to take priority.
* A track record of personally owning meaningful production systems rather than stopping at demos or proofs of concept.
* Strong communication skills and an interest in working directly with domain experts to turn ambiguous real\-world workflows into measurable AI systems.



  





**Why Join?** 




 This is an opportunity to own the entire applied AI feedback loop: defining what a successful investigation looks like, building agents capable of performing that work, and creating the evaluation systems that demonstrate whether those agents are actually reliable.
 



  





 You’ll be tackling a problem where quality goes far beyond benchmark performance. The environment is complex, investigative, and occasionally adversarial, making evaluation, observability, and engineering judgment central to the product rather than an afterthought.
 



  





 The role offers substantial individual ownership and the chance to help define how a growing AI company builds, evaluates, and operates production agent systems from the ground up.
